question: A Government servant is required by CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 to seek prior permission from the Government in some cases. Give the different time limits set for the Competent Authority to grant or refuse permission in respect of some of the provisions of the Rules.

A Government servant is permitted to accept gifts from his near relatives or from personal friend having no official dealings with him on occasions such as weddings anniversaries, funerals or religious functions. Give the maximum limit of the value of gifts on i) occasions as mentioned above, and ii) in other cases.
Write down the important documents that any person driving a commercial vehicle in any public place is required to carry.
Who, according to sub-section (8) section 9 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are the person to whom a Licensing Authority may refuse grant of Driving Licence?
What are the important precautions to be undertaken by a driver of a motor vehicle while approaching an unguarded railway level crossing as per section 131 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

Write down any four circumstances where overtaking is prohibited as mentioned in Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989. OR Who are the person or persons that are included in the meaning of 'Road Users" in Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989?
What are the acts and conducts of Drivers of a motor vehicles that amount to 'Dangerous Driving' for the purpose of section 184 of the Motor Vehicles, Act, 1988?
It is said that 'evidence is the only possible way by which the court can make inferences to render a decision'. Do you agree with the statement? Explain.
A is accused of the murder of B. Discuss the facts which will be in issue at the time of his trial in the court of law.

A was arrested under section 304A of IPC for causing death of X for rash and negligent driving. While in police custody he told B who is not a police officer that he was drunk and that he made no attempt to stop the car while knocking down X. Can the statement of A be admissible as evidence as his confession?
What is the rationale of making dying declaration? Also the write down the essential requirements of a relevant dying declaration.
A sues B for land which is in B's possession. A claims that the land was left to him by the will of C which is B's father. To whom does the burden of proof lies? Explain your answer.
Discuss and illustrate the concept of res gestae as provided in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. To what extent is it admissible in court?

Who may testify as witnesses in trials? Can the following persons testify as witness – (a) lunatic (b) dumb witnesses (c) parties to civil suit (d) judges. Also, A, a client says to his lawyer B 'I wished to obtain possession of property by use of forged deed on which I request you to sue'. Is the communication made by A to his lawyer barred by law from disclosure?
